sentences.zh: 英宗九子。

translations.literal: The Yingzong Emperor had nine sons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yingzong had nine sons.

sentences.zh: 憲宗外，庶三子見湜未封，殤。

translations.literal: Apart from Xianzong, the third son by a concubine, Jian Shi, was not enfeoffed and died young.
translations.idiomatic: Besides the son who became Emperor Xianzong, Yingzong's third son by a concubine, Jian Shi, was never granted a fief and died in infancy.

sentences.zh: 其得封者七王，曰德莊王見潾，曰許悼王見淳，曰秀懷王見澍，曰崇簡王見澤，曰吉簡王見浚，曰忻穆王見治，曰徽莊王見沛。

translations.literal: Those who received enfeoffment were seven princes, namely: Prince Zhuang of De, Jian Lin; Prince Dao of Xu, Jian Chun; Prince Huai of Xiu, Jian Shu; Prince Jian of Chong, Jian Ze; Prince Jian of Ji, Jian Jun; Prince Mu of Xin, Jian Zhi; and Prince Zhuang of Hui, Jian Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Seven sons received princely titles: Zhuang of De (Jian Lin), Dao of Xu (Jian Chun), Huai of Xiu (Jian Shu), Jian of Chong (Jian Ze), Jian of Ji (Jian Jun), Mu of Xin (Jian Zhi), and Zhuang of Hui (Jian Pei).

sentences.zh: 德 莊王見潾，英宗庶二子，天順元年封。成化三年就藩濟南府。正德十二年薨。

translations.literal: De — Prince Zhuang Jian Lin, the Yingzong Emperor's second son by a concubine, was enfeoffed in the first year of Tianshun. In the third year of Chenghua he took up his fief at Jinan Prefecture. He died in the twelfth year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: De princedom — Prince Zhuang Jian Lin, Yingzong's second son by a secondary consort, was enfeoffed in Tianshun 1, took up residence at Jinan Prefecture in Chenghua 3, and died in Zhengde 12.

sentences.zh: 懿王祐榕，莊嫡二子，正德十六年襲封。嘉靖十八年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Yi You Rong, the second legitimate son of Zhuang, inherited the princedom in the sixteenth year of Zhengde. He died in the eighteenth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi You Rong, Zhuang's second son by his primary consort, succeeded in Zhengde 16 and died in Jiajing 18.

sentences.zh: 厚燉，懿庶二子，初封東平王，嘉靖中改封世子。未幾卒。以子載墱襲封，追封王，諡曰懷。

translations.literal: Hou Dun, the second son by a concubine of Yi, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Dongping and in the Jiajing reign was changed to heir. Before long he died. His son Zai Yong inherited the princedom; he was posthumously enfeoffed as prince with the posthumous title Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Dun, Yi's second son by a secondary consort, was first made Prince of Dongping and later named heir in the Jiajing period; he died soon after. His son Zai Yong then inherited the line, and Hou Dun was posthumously raised to princely rank with the title Huai.

sentences.zh: 恭王載墱，懷庶二子，嘉靖二十年襲封。萬曆二年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Gong Zai Yong, the second son by a concubine of Huai, inherited the princedom in the twentieth year of Jiajing. He died in the second year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Gong Zai Yong, Huai's second son by a secondary consort, succeeded in Jiajing 20 and died in Wanli 2.

sentences.zh: 定王翊錧，恭嫡一子，萬曆五年襲封。十六年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Ding Yi Kan, the sole legitimate son of Gong, inherited the princedom in the fifth year of Wanli. He died in the sixteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ding Yi Kan, Gong's only son by his primary consort, inherited the fief in Wanli 5 and died in Wanli 16.

sentences.zh: 王常〈⿱邦清〉，定嫡一子，萬曆十九年襲封。崇禎五年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Chang [bang-qing], the sole legitimate son of Ding, inherited the princedom in the nineteenth year of Wanli. He died in the fifth year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chang Bangqing, Ding's only son by his primary consort, succeeded in Wanli 19 and died in Chongzhen 5.

sentences.zh: 由𣒻，常〈⿱邦清〉庶一子，初封廣宗王，萬曆四十三年改封世子。未襲，卒。 王由樞，常〈⿱邦清〉庶二子，初封郡王，崇禎中進封。十二年正月，大清兵克濟南，見執。

translations.literal: You Kan, the first son by a concubine of Chang [bang-qing], was first enfeoffed as Prince of Guangzong and in the forty-third year of Wanli was changed to heir. He died before inheriting. Prince You Shu, the second son by a concubine of Chang [bang-qing], was first enfeoffed as a commandery prince and was advanced in rank during the Chongzhen reign. In the first month of the twelfth year, Qing forces captured Jinan and he was taken prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: You Kan, Chang Bangqing's eldest son by a secondary consort, was first Prince of Guangzong and named heir in Wanli 43; he died before succeeding. Prince You Shu, Chang's second son by a secondary consort, was first a commandery prince and was promoted during Chongzhen. In the first month of Chongzhen 12, Qing troops took Jinan and captured him.

sentences.zh: 憲宗十四子。

translations.literal: The Xianzong Emperor had fourteen sons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong had fourteen sons.

sentences.zh: 孝宗外，悼恭太子及他皇子俱未名殤。

translations.literal: Apart from Xiaozong, the Dao Gong crown prince and the other imperial sons all died young without being named.
translations.idiomatic: Besides the son who became Emperor Xiaozong, the posthumously titled Crown Prince Dao Gong and the other princes all died in infancy without receiving personal names.

sentences.zh: 其得封者十王，曰興獻王祐杬，曰岐惠王祐棆，曰益端王祐檳，曰衡恭王祐楎，曰雍靖王祐橒，曰壽定王祐榰，曰汝定王祐梈，曰涇簡王祐橓，曰榮莊王祐樞，曰申懿王祐楷。

translations.literal: Those who received enfeoffment were ten princes, namely: Prince Xian of Xing, You Yuan; Prince Hui of Qi, You Lun; Prince Duan of Yi, You Bin; Prince Gong of Heng, You Ge; Prince Jing of Yong, You Yun; Prince Ding of Shou, You Zhi; Prince Ding of Ru, You Bing; Prince Jian of Jing, You Shuan; Prince Zhuang of Rong, You Shu; and Prince Yi of Shen, You Kai.
translations.idiomatic: Ten received princely titles: Xian of Xing (You Yuan), Hui of Qi (You Lun), Duan of Yi (You Bin), Gong of Heng (You Ge), Jing of Yong (You Yun), Ding of Shou (You Zhi), Ding of Ru (You Bing), Jian of Jing (You Shuan), Zhuang of Rong (You Shu), and Yi of Shen (You Kai).

sentences.zh: 興 獻王祐杬，憲宗庶四子，成化二十三年封。弘治七年就藩安陸州。正德十四年薨。後以子嗣大統，追尊獻皇帝，廟號睿宗。

translations.literal: Xing — Prince Xian You Yuan, the Xianzong Emperor's fourth son by a concubine, was enfeoffed in the twenty-third year of Chenghua. In the seventh year of Hongzhi he took up his fief at Anlu. He died in the fourteenth year of Zhengde. Later, because his son succeeded to the great succession, he was posthumously honored as Emperor Xian with the temple name Ruizong.

translations.literal: Guixi — Prince Duan Jing Hou [character], the sixth son by a concubine of Zhuang, was enfeoffed in the tenth year of Jiajing. He died in the ninth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: Guixi — Prince Duan Jing Hou Yi, Zhuang's sixth son by a secondary consort, was enfeoffed in Jiajing 10 and died in Wanli 9.

cells.literal: Guixi — Prince Duan Jing Hou [character], the sixth son by a concubine of Zhuang, was enfeoffed in the tenth year of Jiajing. He died in the ninth year of Wanli.
cells.idiomatic: Guixi — Prince Duan Jing Hou Yi, Zhuang's sixth son by a secondary consort, was enfeoffed in Jiajing 10 and died in Wanli 9.

cells.content: 載堺，端靖嫡一子，嘉靖二十九年封長子。三十一年卒。無子。 王載𤬪，端靖嫡三子，萬曆三十三年以鎮國將軍進封。

translations.literal: Zai Jie, the first legitimate son of Duan Jing, was enfeoffed as heir in the twenty-ninth year of Jiajing. He died in the thirty-first year. He had no sons. Prince Zai [character], the third legitimate son of Duan Jing, was advanced from Defender-General of the State in the thirty-third year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: Zai Jie, Duan Jing's first son by his primary consort, was named heir in Jiajing 29 and died in Jiajing 31 without sons. Prince Zai Yi, Duan Jing's third son by his primary consort, was promoted from Defender-General of the State in Wanli 33.

cells.content: 肇慶 王由楨，常溒嫡五子，天啟六年封。

translations.literal: Zhaoqing — Prince You Zhen, the fifth legitimate son of Chang Shuang, was enfeoffed in the sixth year of Tianqi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoqing — Prince You Zhen, Chang Shuang's fifth son by his primary consort, was enfeoffed in Tianqi 6.

cells.literal: Zhaoqing — Prince You Zhen, the fifth legitimate son of Chang Shuang, was enfeoffed in the sixth year of Tianqi.
cells.idiomatic: Zhaoqing — Prince You Zhen, Chang Shuang's fifth son by his primary consort, was enfeoffed in Tianqi 6.
cells.translation: Zhaoqing — Prince You Zhen, Chang Shuang's fifth son by his primary consort, was enfeoffed in Tianqi 6.

cells.content: 申 懿王祐楷，憲宗庶十四子，弘治四年封，建邸敍州府。十六年未就藩，薨。無子，封除。

translations.literal: Shen — Prince Yi You Kai, the Xianzong Emperor's fourteenth son by a concubine, was enfeoffed in the fourth year of Hongzhi and a residence was built at Xuzhou Prefecture. He died in the sixteenth year without having taken up his fief. He had no sons, and the enfeoffment was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Shen princedom — Prince Yi You Kai, Xianzong's fourteenth son by a secondary consort, was enfeoffed in Hongzhi 4 with a mansion at Xuzhou but died in Hongzhi 16 before going to his fief, leaving no heirs; the title was abolished.

cells.literal: Shen — Prince Yi You Kai, the Xianzong Emperor's fourteenth son by a concubine, was enfeoffed in the fourth year of Hongzhi and a residence was built at Xuzhou Prefecture. He died in the sixteenth year without having taken up his fief. He had no sons, and the enfeoffment was abolished.

sentences.zh: 世宗八子。

translations.literal: The Shizong Emperor had eight sons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong had eight sons.

sentences.zh: 穆宗外，哀沖、莊敬二太子及他皇子俱殤。

translations.literal: Apart from Muzong, the Ai Chong and Zhuang Jing crown princes and the other imperial sons all died young.
translations.idiomatic: Besides the son who became Emperor Muzong, the crown princes Ai Chong and Zhuang Jing and the other princes all died in infancy.

sentences.zh: 其得封者一王，曰景恭王載圳。

translations.literal: The one who received enfeoffment was a single prince, namely Prince Gong of Jing, Zai Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Only one received a princely title: Gong of Jing (Zai Zhen).

sentences.zh: 景 恭王載圳，世宗庶四子，嘉靖十八年封。四十年就藩德安府。四十四年薨。無子，封除。

translations.literal: Jing — Prince Gong Zai Zhen, the Shizong Emperor's fourth son by a concubine, was enfeoffed in the eighteenth year of Jiajing. In the fortieth year he took up his fief at De'an Prefecture. He died in the forty-fourth year. He had no sons, and the enfeoffment was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Jing princedom — Prince Gong Zai Zhen, Shizong's fourth son by a secondary consort, was enfeoffed in Jiajing 18, took up residence at De'an Prefecture in Jiajing 40, and died in Jiajing 44 without heirs; the title was abolished.

sentences.zh: 穆宗四子。

translations.literal: The Muzong Emperor had four sons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Muzong had four sons.

sentences.zh: 神宗外，憲懷太子及他皇子殤。

translations.literal: Apart from Shenzong, the Xian Huai crown prince and the other imperial sons died young.
translations.idiomatic: Besides the son who became Emperor Shenzong, Crown Prince Xian Huai and the other princes died in infancy.

sentences.zh: 其得封者一王，曰潞簡王翊鏐。

translations.literal: The one who received enfeoffment was a single prince, namely Prince Jian of Lu, Yi Liu.
translations.idiomatic: Only one received a princely title: Jian of Lu (Yi Liu).

sentences.zh: 潞 簡王翊鏐，穆宗嫡四子，隆慶五年封。萬曆十七年就藩衞輝府。四十二年薨。

translations.literal: Lu — Prince Jian Yi Liu, the Muzong Emperor's fourth legitimate son, was enfeoffed in the fifth year of Longqing. In the seventeenth year of Wanli he took up his fief at Weihui Prefecture. He died in the forty-second year.
translations.idiomatic: Lu princedom — Prince Jian Yi Liu, Muzong's fourth son by his primary consort, was enfeoffed in Longqing 5, took up residence at Weihui Prefecture in Wanli 17, and died in Wanli 42.

sentences.zh: 王常淓，簡庶一子，萬曆四十六年襲封。後以國亡，寓杭州。大清順治二年六月，王師至，遂降。

translations.literal: Prince Chang Fen, the sole son by a concubine of Jian, inherited the princedom in the forty-sixth year of Wanli. Later, when the state perished, he lodged at Hangzhou. In the sixth month of the second year of Shunzhi under the Great Qing, the royal army arrived and he surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Chang Fen, Jian's only son by a secondary consort, succeeded in Wanli 46. After the dynasty fell he took refuge in Hangzhou; when Qing forces reached the city in the sixth month of Shunzhi 2, he surrendered.

cells.content: 寶豐 王常𰛭，簡庶二子，天啟三年封。

translations.literal: Baofeng — Prince Chang [character], the second son by a concubine of Jian, was enfeoffed in the third year of Tianqi.
translations.idiomatic: Baofeng — Prince Chang Yi, Jian's second son by a secondary consort, was enfeoffed in Tianqi 3.

cells.literal: Baofeng — Prince Chang [character], the second son by a concubine of Jian, was enfeoffed in the third year of Tianqi.
cells.idiomatic: Baofeng — Prince Chang Yi, Jian's second son by a secondary consort, was enfeoffed in Tianqi 3.
cells.translation: Baofeng — Prince Chang Yi, Jian's second son by a secondary consort, was enfeoffed in Tianqi 3.

sentences.zh: 神宗八子。

translations.literal: The Shenzong Emperor had eight sons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong had eight sons.

sentences.zh: 光宗外，三子未封。

translations.literal: Apart from Guangzong, three sons were not enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: Besides the son who became Emperor Guangzong, three sons received no princely titles.

sentences.zh: 其得封者四王，曰福恭王常洵，曰瑞王常浩，曰惠王常潤，曰桂端王常瀛。

translations.literal: Those who received enfeoffment were four princes, namely: Prince Gong of Fu, Chang Xun; Prince of Rui, Chang Hao; Prince of Hui, Chang Run; and Prince Duan of Gui, Chang Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Four received princely titles: Gong of Fu (Chang Xun), Rui (Chang Hao), Hui (Chang Run), and Duan of Gui (Chang Ying).

sentences.zh: 福 恭王常洵，神宗庶三子，萬曆二十九年封。四十二年就藩河南府。崇禎十四年正月，闖賊陷洛陽，遇害。

translations.literal: Fu — Prince Gong Chang Xun, the Shenzong Emperor's third son by a concubine, was enfeoffed in the twenty-ninth year of Wanli. In the forty-second year he took up his fief at Henan Prefecture. In the first month of the fourteenth year of Chongzhen, the roving-bandit forces took Luoyang and he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Fu princedom — Prince Gong Chang Xun, Shenzong's third son by a secondary consort, was enfeoffed in Wanli 29 and took up residence at Henan Prefecture in Wanli 42. In the first month of Chongzhen 14, Li Zicheng's rebels seized Luoyang and killed him.

sentences.zh: 由崧，恭庶一子，萬曆四十五年封德昌王。崇禎十六年襲封。十七年，闖賊陷京師，五月自立於南京，僭號弘光。大清順治二年五月，王師渡江，被執。

translations.literal: You Song, the sole son by a concubine of Gong, was enfeoffed as Prince of Dechang in the forty-fifth year of Wanli. He inherited the princedom in the sixteenth year of Chongzhen. In the seventeenth year the roving-bandit forces took the capital; in the fifth month he declared himself at Nanjing and usurped the reign title Hongguang. In the fifth month of the second year of Shunzhi under the Great Qing, the royal army crossed the Yangzi and he was captured.
translations.idiomatic: You Song, Gong's only son by a secondary consort, was made Prince of Dechang in Wanli 45 and succeeded in Chongzhen 16. When rebels took Beijing in Chongzhen 17, he proclaimed himself at Nanjing in the fifth month with the reign title Hongguang. Qing forces crossed the Yangzi in the fifth month of Shunzhi 2 and captured him.

cells.content: 潁上 王由榘，恭庶二子，萬曆中封。崇禎十四年正月與恭王同遇害。

translations.literal: Yingshang — Prince You Ju, the second son by a concubine of Gong, was enfeoffed during the Wanli reign. In the first month of the fourteenth year of Chongzhen he was killed together with Prince Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Yingshang — Prince You Ju, Gong's second son by a secondary consort, was enfeoffed in the Wanli period and was killed alongside Prince Gong in the first month of Chongzhen 14.

cells.literal: Yingshang — Prince You Ju, the second son by a concubine of Gong, was enfeoffed during the Wanli reign. In the first month of the fourteenth year of Chongzhen he was killed together with Prince Gong.
cells.idiomatic: Yingshang — Prince You Ju, Gong's second son by a secondary consort, was enfeoffed in the Wanli period and was killed alongside Prince Gong in the first month of Chongzhen 14.

cells.content: 瑞 王常浩，神宗庶五子，萬曆二十九年封。天啟七年就藩漢中府。崇禎十七年，張獻忠陷重慶，遇害。

translations.literal: Rui — Prince Chang Hao, the Shenzong Emperor's fifth son by a concubine, was enfeoffed in the twenty-ninth year of Wanli. In the seventh year of Tianqi he took up his fief at Hanzhong Prefecture. In the seventeenth year of Chongzhen, Zhang Xianzhong took Chongqing and he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Rui princedom — Prince Chang Hao, Shenzong's fifth son by a secondary consort, was enfeoffed in Wanli 29 and took up residence at Hanzhong Prefecture in Tianqi 7. In Chongzhen 17, Zhang Xianzhong seized Chongqing and killed him.

cells.literal: Rui — Prince Chang Hao, the Shenzong Emperor's fifth son by a concubine, was enfeoffed in the twenty-ninth year of Wanli. In the seventh year of Tianqi he took up his fief at Hanzhong Prefecture. In the seventeenth year of Chongzhen, Zhang Xianzhong took Chongqing and he was killed.

cells.content: 惠 王常潤，神宗庶六子，萬曆二十九年封。天啟七年就藩荊州府。崇禎末，奔廣州府。大清順治三年，廣東平，被執，死。

translations.literal: Hui — Prince Chang Run, the Shenzong Emperor's sixth son by a concubine, was enfeoffed in the twenty-ninth year of Wanli. In the seventh year of Tianqi he took up his fief at Jingzhou Prefecture. At the end of the Chongzhen reign he fled to Guangzhou Prefecture. In the third year of Shunzhi under the Great Qing, when Guangdong was pacified, he was captured and died.
translations.idiomatic: Hui princedom — Prince Chang Run, Shenzong's sixth son by a secondary consort, was enfeoffed in Wanli 29 and took up his fief at Jingzhou in Tianqi 7. In the final years of Chongzhen he fled to Guangzhou; when Guangdong was pacified in Shunzhi 3 he was captured and died.

cells.content: 桂 端王常瀛，神宗庶七子，萬曆二十九年封。天啟七年就藩衡州府。崇禎十六年，獻賊陷衡州，王由永州入廣西，寄居蒼梧。十七年薨。

translations.literal: Gui — Prince Duan Chang Ying, the Shenzong Emperor's seventh son by a concubine, was enfeoffed in the twenty-ninth year of Wanli. In the seventh year of Tianqi he took up his fief at Hengzhou Prefecture. In the sixteenth year of Chongzhen, the rebel Xian took Hengzhou; the prince entered Guangxi from Yongzhou and lodged at Cangwu. He died in the seventeenth year.
translations.idiomatic: Gui princedom — Prince Duan Chang Ying, Shenzong's seventh son by a secondary consort, was enfeoffed in Wanli 29 and took up residence at Hengzhou in Tianqi 7. In Chongzhen 16, Zhang Xianzhong's forces took Hengzhou; the prince fled from Yongzhou into Guangxi and stayed at Cangwu. He died in Chongzhen 17.

cells.content: 由𣜬，端嫡三子，初封安仁王。唐王聿鍵自立，偽封為桂王。大清順治三年，卒於梧州。無子。 由榔，端嫡四子，初封永明王。大清順治三年，福建平，由榔自立於肇慶，僭號永曆。是冬，王師度嶺，由榔走廣西，自是走貴州，又走雲南，遂入緬甸。十八年冬，王師至，緬人獻之。明年，殺諸雲南。

translations.literal: You [character], the third legitimate son of Duan, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Anren. When the Prince of Tang, Yujian, declared himself, he was falsely enfeoffed as Prince of Gui. He died at Wuzhou in the third year of Shunzhi under the Great Qing. He had no sons. You Lang, the fourth legitimate son of Duan, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Yongming. In the third year of Shunzhi, when Fujian was pacified, You Lang declared himself at Zhaoqing and usurped the reign title Yongli. That winter the royal army crossed the ranges; You Lang fled to Guangxi, then to Guizhou, then to Yunnan, and finally entered Burma. In the winter of the eighteenth year the royal army arrived and the Burmese handed him over. The next year he was executed in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: You Yi, Duan's third son by his primary consort, was first Prince of Anren; when the Prince of Tang, Yujian, declared himself, he was falsely made Prince of Gui. He died at Wuzhou in Shunzhi 3 without sons. You Lang, Duan's fourth son by his primary consort, was first Prince of Yongming. After Fujian was pacified in Shunzhi 3, he proclaimed himself at Zhaoqing with the reign title Yongli. That winter Qing troops crossed the Nanling; he fled through Guangxi, Guizhou, and Yunnan into Burma. Qing forces reached Burma in the winter of Shunzhi 18; the Burmese surrendered him, and he was executed in Yunnan the following year.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝七子。

translations.literal: The Chonglie Emperor had seven sons.
translations.idiomatic: The Chongzhen Emperor had seven sons.

sentences.zh: 獻愍太子慈烺外，嫡第二子，庶第五子、第六子、第七子俱殤。

translations.literal: Apart from the Xian Min crown prince Cilang, the second legitimate son and the fifth, sixth, and seventh sons by concubines all died young.
translations.idiomatic: Besides Crown Prince Xian Min Cilang, the second son by the primary consort and the fifth, sixth, and seventh sons by secondary consorts all died in infancy.

sentences.zh: 其封而未建藩邸者二王，曰定哀王慈炯，曰永悼王慈炤。

translations.literal: Two who were enfeoffed but for whom princely residences were not built were: Prince Ai of Ding, Ci Jiong, and Prince Dao of Yong, Ci Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Two received titles but never established fiefs: Ai of Ding (Ci Jiong) and Dao of Yong (Ci Zhao).

sentences.zh: 定 哀王慈炯，莊烈帝嫡三子，崇禎十四年封，未建藩邸。十七年，闖賊陷京師，被執，不知所終。

translations.literal: Ding — Prince Ai Ci Jiong, the Chonglie Emperor's third legitimate son, was enfeoffed in the fourteenth year of Chongzhen; no princely residence was built. In the seventeenth year the roving-bandit forces took the capital; he was captured and his end is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Ding — Prince Ai Ci Jiong, the Chongzhen Emperor's third son by his primary consort, was enfeoffed in Chongzhen 14 but never went to a fief. When rebels took Beijing in Chongzhen 17 he was captured; his fate is unknown.

cells.content: 永 悼王慈炤，莊烈帝庶四子，崇禎十五年封，未建藩邸。十七年，闖賊陷京師，被執，不知所終。

translations.literal: Yong — Prince Dao Ci Zhao, the Chonglie Emperor's fourth son by a concubine, was enfeoffed in the fifteenth year of Chongzhen; no princely residence was built. In the seventeenth year the roving-bandit forces took the capital; he was captured and his end is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Yong — Prince Dao Ci Zhao, the Chongzhen Emperor's fourth son by a secondary consort, was enfeoffed in Chongzhen 15 but never went to a fief. When rebels took Beijing in Chongzhen 17 he was captured; his fate is unknown.
